import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Set a professional and visually appealing style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a pair plot, which is excellent for visualizing relationships
# between variables in a dataset. We color by 'species' to see how the
# measurements separate the different types of iris flowers.
g = sns.pairplot(
    df,
    hue='species',
    diag_kind='kde',  # Use Kernel Density Estimation on the diagonals
    markers=["o", "s", "D"],
    plot_kws={'alpha': 0.85, 's': 50, 'edgecolor': 'k'},
    diag_kws={'linewidth': 2, 'shade': True}
)

# Add a clear, descriptive title to the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle(
    'Relationships Between Sepal & Petal Measurements by Iris Species',
    y=1.02,  # Adjust title position to be slightly above the plot
    fontsize=16,
    fontweight='bold'
)

# Improve individual axis labels for clarity
# Seaborn's defaults are good, but we can be more explicit.
g.axes[0,0].set_ylabel('Sepal Length (cm)')
g.axes[1,0].set_ylabel('Sepal Width (cm)')
g.axes[2,0].set_ylabel('Petal Length (cm)')
g.axes[3,0].set_ylabel('Petal Width (cm)')

g.axes[3,0].set_xlabel('Sepal Length (cm)')

g.axes[3,3].set_xlabel('Petal Width (cm)')

)

# Add a clear, descriptive title to the entire figure

    'Relationships Between Sepal & Petal Measurements by Iris Species',
    y=1.02,  # Adjust title position to be slightly above the plot

    fontweight='bold'
